definition: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated at batch size 1 generating the longest-prompt test hunk (527 tokens), 4-bit NF4 text-only base + unmerged LoRA r16, greedy, max_new 768 (pre-registered); GB = 1e9 bytes

weights.note: tied fp16 embedding/lm_head alone is ~1.02 GB of this

kaggle_t4.source: kaggle/level4/out/qwen (first call, scored run) and kaggle/level4/out/l4mem/out/memdiag.json (staged diagnostic)

diagnosis: On the T4 the first generate call in a fresh process peaks at 2.170 GB (reproduced to the byte in the scored run and in the diagnostic; cause unidentified, a ~0.3 GB transient above the 1.853 GB load). Repeating the same prompt later peaks at 1.942 GB. A chunked-prefill forward pass late in the same process (new input shapes) peaks at 2.162 GB again, and a forward pass materialising logits for all 527 positions peaks at 2.152 GB on both GPUs, so the transient may re-appear for new shapes: the steady-state figure has only been verified for a repeated identical prompt. Locally (RTX 3050), varied prompts of 201-527 tokens all peak at 1.92-1.94 GB with no first-call transient (reviewer check). Explicit logits_to_keep=1 changed nothing.
reading: Weights + adapter 1.85 GB. Steady-state inference peak 1.93-1.94 GB where verified (passes < 2 GB, 3% margin). Cold first call on a T4: 2.17 GB, an 8.5% miss. Whole-process GPU memory including the CUDA context: nvidia-smi 1,997 MiB (= 2.09 GB) locally and 2,539 MiB (= 2.66 GB) on Kaggle, i.e. over 2 GB in decimal units.
